definitions.gloss: loanword, borrowed word, word of foreign origin
definitions.explanation: A word adopted from a foreign language into Japanese. In practice, this term usually refers to words borrowed from Western languages (especially English), which are written in katakana. Words borrowed from Chinese ({漢語|かんご}) are generally not called {外来語|がいらいご}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{外来語|がいらいご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: There are many loanwords in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 「⟦コンピュータ→コンピュータ：01992_konpyuuta⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{外来語|がいらいご}だ。

⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{外来語|がいらいご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}え→増える：01183_fueru⟧すぎて、⟦{年配|ねんぱい}→年配：10432_nenpai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{分|わ}かり→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧にくい⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Some say that loanwords have increased so much recently that they are hard for older people to understand.

notes:
USAGE:
Japanese vocabulary is classified into three categories: ⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧ (native Japanese words), ⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧ (Sino-Japanese words from Chinese), and {外来語|がいらいご} (loanwords from other languages). Despite Chinese being technically "foreign," {外来語|がいらいご} conventionally excludes ⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧ and refers mainly to Western borrowings written in katakana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外来語|がいらいご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: use a loanword
- ⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{外来語|がいらいご}: loanword from English
- {外来語|がいらいご}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: loanword dictionary
- {外来語|がいらいご}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{乱用|らんよう}→乱用：15259_ranyou⟧: overuse of loanwords

SIMILAR WORDS:
{外来語|がいらいご} is the standard linguistic term. カタカナ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (katakana word) is a casual synonym. ⟦{借用語|しゃくようご}→借用語：19051_shakuyougo⟧ (borrowed word) is the more technical linguistic term.
